post.description: Device authorization (RFC 8628, §3.1): a machine without a browser asks for a device code and a user code. Its person approves the user code on the verification page, `GET /device`, within `expires_in` seconds, the server setting `--device-code-lifetime`; the machine meanwhile polls `POST /auth/token` every `interval` seconds, the server setting `--device-poll-interval`.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`application/problem+json`), or the request (`application/json`, RFC 6749, §5.2): `invalid_request` without a `client_id` or with one twice, `invalid_client` with another `client_id`.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to GitHub's authorization page, asking for no scope, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from GitHub. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the app's client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier and reads the GitHub user. The first sign-in of a GitHub user creates an account with the user's GitHub ID as its GitHub sign-in method; later ones reach the account that holds that method and update the method's GitHub login. Keeps no GitHub token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/github/link`, it adds the GitHub sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

parameters.description: GitHub's error, such as `access_denied`, instead of a code.

200.description: Signed in or linked: a page that sends the browser to the return page. For a link whose request lacks the cookie of the web session that started it, as one from another site lacks the `SameSite=Strict` cookie, first, once, a page that opens this callback again from this server.

Set-Cookie.description: Signed in: the session cookie `skald_session`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` under an https public URL; signed in or linked: the removal of the cookie that bound `state`.

Sends the browser to GitHub as `GET /auth/github` does, with a `state` that also binds the link to this web session; GitHub comes back through `GET /auth/github/callback`. The link works only while the session lasts.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to Google's authorization endpoint, by OpenID Connect's authorization code flow, asking for the scopes `openid` and `email` only, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and a `nonce` and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`. The server reads Google's metadata from its issuer, the setting `--google-issuer`, at the first sign-in start that reaches it.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of this server to return to once signed in: a path such as `/settings?tab=devices`. Anything else, such as another site's address, returns to `/`.

Location.description: Google's authorization endpoint with the client ID, the redirect URI `<public URL>/auth/google/callback`, `response_type=code`, the scopes `openid email`, `state`, `nonce`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` under an https public URL, for the callback's path only.

502.description: Google is unreachable, or its metadata or keys are malformed.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from Google. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier, and checks the ID token as OpenID Connect Core 1.0, §3.1.3.7, says, with this sign-in's `nonce`. The account is bound to its Google sign-in method, Google's issuer and the ID token's `sub`, never to the email. The first sign-in creates the account, its username made from the email's local part; later ones reach the account that holds that method, also after the email changes. Keeps no email, ID token or Google token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/google/link`, it adds the Google sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

Set-Cookie.description: Signed in: the session cookie `skald_session`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` under an https public URL; signed in or linked: the removal of the cookie that bound `state`.

post.summary: Poll for a device flow's session token
post.description: The token endpoint (RFC 8628, §3.4): the machine polls with its device code, at most once per `interval` seconds, until its person approves or denies the user code or the codes expire. An approved code gives a session token once; every later poll for it answers `invalid_grant`.

200.description: The person approved the user code: the session token for their account.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`application/problem+json`), or gives no token (`application/json`, RFC 8628, §3.5): `authorization_pending` until the person decides; `slow_down` to a poll less than `interval` seconds after the previous one; `access_denied` once the person denied the code; `expired_token` once the codes expired; `invalid_grant` for an unknown device code or one that already gave its token; `invalid_request`, `invalid_client` or `unsupported_grant_type` for a malformed request.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

get.description: Opened by the person's browser at `verification_uri` or `verification_uri_complete`. It works while the server has the settings of any provider. With a web session, whatever sign-in method started it, it names the account's username, says that approving signs a machine in to that account and asks for the user code, filled in from `user_code`, with the buttons Approve and Deny, which submit `POST /device`. Opening it decides nothing.

post.summary: Approve or deny a user code
post.description: Submitted by the verification page's form, with the web session's cookie, from a page of this server: a request whose `Origin` is another site's, or that has none, decides nothing. Approving binds the code to the session's account; a user code works once, for one account. After 10 wrong, used or expired codes within 15 minutes, the account's codes, right ones included, are refused until fewer remain in that window.
